# Test 20261006-073147-23d8: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:5; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:16 | `shop.refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-02A75B", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. Rule 3 says, "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." The code compares `amount_eur` directly with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`. It recorded this refund without an approval request. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:6; trace.jsonl:5; app.py:67 | The reply says the refund "should appear on your card within 1-2 business days." The tool returned only the refund ID, amount and `"status": "paid"`. No rule or tool result supplies a settlement time. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:8; trace.jsonl:6; app.py:64; state.json:16 | The reply says, "Your refund of €80 is complete and paid to your card." Turn 2 also claims the card as the destination. The tool only records a refund in the local state. Neither its result nor the state identifies a card or confirms a card payment. The local refund record supports completion within the app, but not payment to a card. |

## Notes

I read the transcript with trace, each trace item, findings.json, audit.json, manifest.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py and the current state.json. I also searched the project tests and read the relevant evaluation-example text. That example describes an earlier app with a separate approval tool; the tested app has only lookup_order and refund. I judged this test against its own code and rules.

The findings list is empty. The audit reports no breaks, errors or changed turn text. These checks do not establish that the app followed its business rules. The order lookup agrees with the tool result and current state. The refund ID and amount agree with state.json, which has no approvals entry. I did not report a state mismatch for the local refund completion claim.

The recorded app model session used Claude Code 2.1.286 (findings.json). The manifest records Claude Code 2.1.290 (Claude Code), Codex codex-cli 0.160.0 and verbatim-relay 0.1.0. These are distinct version records; I did not assume the manifest's CLI version was the app session version.

I used read-only commands for the evaluation and wrote only this report. I did not start the app, call its tools, send it a message or run tests that could change state. I could not verify an external card transaction, a settlement date, delivery dates or customer ownership from these records. This test provides no evidence of a return-window or order-privacy breach.
